```python
# Unit test for function reverse_delete
def test_reverse_delete():
    # Basic cases: characters removed, result not a palindrome
    assert reverse_delete("abcde", "ae") == ('bcd', False)
    assert reverse_delete("abcdef", "b") == ('acdef', False)
    assert reverse_delete("dwik", "w") == ('dik', False)
    assert reverse_delete("vba", "v") == ('ba', False)
    assert reverse_delete("frank", "m") == ('frank', False)

    # Result is a palindrome after deletion
    assert reverse_delete("abcdedcba", "ab") == ('cdedc', True)
    assert reverse_delete("mjm", "m") == ('j', True)

    # Deleting all characters yields empty string (trivially a palindrome)
    assert reverse_delete("a", "a") == ('', True)
    assert reverse_delete("abc", "abc") == ('', True)

    # No characters deleted (c has chars not in s, or c is empty)
    assert reverse_delete("abcdedcba", "") == ('abcdedcba', True)
    assert reverse_delete("abcdedcba", "v") == ('abcdedcba', True)
    assert reverse_delete("hello", "xyz") == ('hello', False)

    # Single character strings
    assert reverse_delete("a", "") == ('a', True)
    assert reverse_delete("a", "b") == ('a', True)

    # Multiple occurrences of characters to delete
    assert reverse_delete("aaabbbccc", "b") == ('aaaccc', False)
    assert reverse_delete("racecar", "r") == ('aceca', True)

    # Case sensitivity check
    assert reverse_delete("Aa", "a") == ('A', True)

    print("All test_reverse_delete tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_reverse_delete()
```
